messages:
marina: Heads-up, my perf run on canary shows FP8 path regressed ~25% vs yesterday. Tokens/s went from ~4200 -> ~3100 on sm90 with CUTLASS FP8 kernels :thinking_face:
marina: Repro command: `./bench_perf --model=gpt-3-small --seq=1024 --batch=4 --quant=fp8 --kernel=cutlass --arch=sm90 --kv-cache=true`
marina: Attached profiler snippet (top lines):
```
GPU time breakdown: kernel_execute 68%, memcpy_h2d 12%, memcpy_d2h 3%, kernel_launch_overhead 10%, other 7%
CUTLASS FP8 kernel: avg_latency 1.9ms, throughput drop vs INT8 was surprising
KV cache hitrate: 92% (prefix reuse)
Batcher: avg waiting time 6.2ms, batch size distribution skewed to 1-2
```
aj: :eyes: did you see extra memcpy from calibration step? FP8 calibration path inserts a cast+repack on the weights sometimes.
marina: yes I noticed a short stage labeled `quant_calib_repack` in the timeline, ~8% of time. If that happens on every request it's bad.
sam: any difference when forcing `--kernel=triton`? CUTLASS has a fallback path for some conv shapes that forces extra workspace allocs.
marina: good idea. I ran `--kernel=triton` earlier and saw tokens/s ~3950 (so still slightly down vs baseline but much closer).
devon: can you paste the binary build flags used for the CUTLASS artifact? I want to check if we accidentally toggled `-DCUTLASS_USE_TENSOR_CORE_INT8` or similar.
marina: build meta: `nvcc -arch=sm_90 -O3 -lineinfo -DCUTLASS_ALLOW_4BIT=1 -DENABLE_FP8=1 -DARCH_PROBER=v2`
kevin: hm, `-DARCH_PROBER=v2` changed arch detection heuristics last week. Might cause us to pick a different kernel variant that does extra workspace copies for alignment.
aj: also check if `KERNEL_PREFETCH=1` was enabled at runtime; prefetch in CUTLASS can marshal data differently.
sam: I'll attach pprof and nvprof traces to the infra job. infra-bot: Collected traces and uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/job-1769951234/traces.tar.gz (job id perf-176995).
marina: thanks infra-bot.
devon: plan: 1) bisect arch-prober change locally, 2) force compile without `ARCH_PROBER=v2` and compare, 3) run small microbench for FP8 copy-free kernel if available. Assigning to me and aj.
aj: I'll also try toggling `--kv-cache=false` to see whether KV cache interaction is amplifying the memcpy. If disabling KV makes FP8 recover, then it's an interplay.
marina: quick config snippet I used for the bench (in case it helps):
```
{
  "batcher": {"max_latency_ms": 20, "max_batch_size": 8, "strategy": "latency-first"},
  "runtime": {"kernel_priority": ["cutlass","triton"], "quant_mode": "prefer_fp8"}
}
```
sam: also collect tiny repro with `--seq=128 --batch=16` to stress throughput/batching differences.
kevin: note: recent commit 4c9b2 toggled `CUTLASS_ALIGN_WORKSPACE` default to true — that can add a memcopy to align to 128B lanes. Worth checking.
marina: action items done: uploaded raw logs to the perf bucket and started bisect. I'll post intermediate numbers here.
aj: if we confirm it's the arch probe, we should add a runtime override to force older probe and add a flaky feature flag for canary.
devon: agreed. also add a perf test that runs FP8 microbench in CI so this doesn't slip.
marina: OK, first bisect result: disabling `ARCH_PROBER=v2` recovers tokens/s to ~4100. So that's the culprit. More details in the bisect notes I'm uploading.
sam: :tada: nice find. Next: narrow which heuristic in v2 causes repacking (alignment vs tiling choice).
kevin: I'll open a short PR to add a runtime switch `REDWOOD_ARCH_PROBE=legacy|v2` and default to v2 but allow canary to override. Link when ready.
marina: great. marking this thread for follow-up after kevin's PR and devon/aj perf CI test. Thanks all.
